newsitem.title: USA: Century to cut some production, workforce.
newsitem.headline: Century to cut some production, workforce.

text.p: Century Aluminum Co on Tuesday said it plans to cut production of sheet products by 20 percent and cut its workforce by 10 percent.
Century said the moves are part of a new operating plan meant to improve the financial performance of its Ravenswood operations and are expected to cost between $4 million and $5 million.
"A large portion of the cost of the program will be taken as a charge in the third quarter," company spokesman Alfred Posti said.
Posti said the company did not have an exact estimate of the charge.

The Ravenswood operations in West Virginia are Century's only fabricated alu,minum plant and has 2,200 employees. It has capacity to produce 168,000-metric tons per year of primary aluminum and its mills have capacity to roll 270,000 mtpy of aluminum sheet and plate.

Cutting sheet production would reduce overall volume 20 percent, or about 55,000 metric tons a year. THe move would be focused on low-margin, commodity products and would begin in the fourth quarter and be completed by year's end 1998, the company said.
It said it believes the 10-percent reduction in employment can be done through early retirement incentives and said it also plans to streamline its rolled products organization.
